observation: Two defects in the self-shape runner are invisible in CI and only appear when a run is repeated over existing state. The runner pinned `--contract-revision 1` when recording its validation observation. That is correct on a fresh CI checkout, where the Contract is always at revision 1, and wrong the moment a Contract is revised: the observation attaches to a superseded revision and `workflow close` then reports '[FAIL] validation: validation evidence missing or not passed for: composer ci (no evidence)' with nothing naming the revision as the cause. Separately, a run that fails part-way leaves its governed Session active, and every later run then dies at '[FAIL] workflow plan: Cannot revise Contract for SELF-SHAPE while a governed Session is active.' The runner offers no recovery; the operator has to know that `session close <id> --status dropped` is the way out.

evidence.summary: `workflow status SELF-SHAPE --format json` reported references.contract.revision 2 while the runner recorded its observation against revision 1. The close gate's message named the command, not the revision, so the cause was only found by reading the manifest.
First attempt aborted on an unrelated composer.lock error; the next two attempts failed immediately on the leftover active Session, one per stale session, until each was closed by hand.

After reading the approved revision from workflow status instead of assuming it, the full run passed end to end: 'Self-shape dogfood: PASSED', including workflow close and the post-prune projection replay.

hypothesis: A constant that is right in the only environment a gate normally runs in will not be questioned. CI always starts from a fresh checkout, so revision 1 was true every time it mattered, and the assumption survived precisely because the dogfood never ran twice over the same state.
validated_conclusion: A runner asks the workflow for durable identity rather than assuming it; a value that CI always makes true is an assumption, not a fact. When a gate refuses evidence, its message names the property that failed to match - a revision, a compilation - and not only the command, or the failure is diagnosed by reading manifests by hand.
